messages:
Priya (Support): FYI customer (Acme Mobile) reports 401 invalid_api_key after a recent deploy. They say the same key used to work. curl returns {"error":"invalid_api_key"}. Repro steps below.

Priya (Support): ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer |ABCDefGhIjKlMnOPqrsT==" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
# {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
```

Jordan (Eng): can you paste the exact Authorization header as it reached our servers (raw)?

Priya (Support): raw header captured from customer logs: `Authorization: Bearer |ABCDefGhIjKlMnOPqrsT==`

Jordan (Eng): that leading `|` looks like a prefix got injected. where is the key sourced from in their pipeline?

Priya (Support): they said it comes from a protected CI variable in their .gitlab-ci.yml and is written into a file during the deploy job. they shared the pipeline snippet: `SECRET_KEY: |
  |ABCDefGhIjKlMnOPqrsT==` (they used a YAML literal block when templating the var).

Jordan (Eng): ah — if the job export step reuses the literal block marker or the templating step concatenates the marker into the value you can end up with a leading `|`. some runners/templaters don't strip that when you pass through envfiles. quick check: ask them to run `echo -n "$SECRET_KEY" | xxd` in a job to see raw bytes.

Maya (Security): immediate recommendations: rotate the compromised key (do it now), revoke the old key, and confirm no production requests used the leaked value after rotation. we'll mark the old key as revoked and scan recent logs for the `|ABCDef` prefix. :lock:

Priya (Support): customer just rotated and confirmed new key works. they want remediation steps for CI so this doesn't happen again.

Jordan (Eng): remediation notes to give them:
1) Avoid YAML literal blocks for secret values when storing/templating; store as a single-line raw secret.
2) When writing to files in CI use `printf '%s' "$SECRET_KEY" > /path/to/creds` or `echo -n "$SECRET_KEY"` (avoid commands that preserve extra markers).
3) Add a validation step: `if [[ "$SECRET_KEY" =~ ^[^A-Za-z0-9] ]]; then echo "bad secret prefix" && exit 1; fi`

Jordan (Eng): grep-finder for other repos: `git grep -n "^\s*[A-Z0-9_]*:\s*\|" || true` will find YAML keys defined with `|` markers you should audit.

infra-bot: api-key-activity: old key last seen 2024-11-02T12:34:56Z, revoked by customer at 2024-11-02T12:40:12Z.

Maya (Security): also remind them to mark CI variables as protected and restrict runner access. recommend rotating any downstream tokens that may have been derived from the leaked key. :thumbsup:

Priya (Support): customer confirmed tests pass and they patched the CI templating. closing on our side, will follow up with a short postmortem they can share internally. :white_check_mark:
